algorithm_reference.exact_property: closest rational with denominator not exceeding M; tie smaller denominator, then lower rational if both denominators equal
algorithm_reference.note: The standalone witness also independently verifies the optimum by enumerating all denominators in bounded cases, not merely testing an equivalent implementation against itself.

candidate.kind: pure deterministic relation over exact rational values
args: x: exact rational with reduced signed numerator and positive denominator
candidate.result: Reduced signed numerator and positive denominator p/q with 1 <= q <= M
candidate.law: Choose the closest rational p/q to x under denominator <= M, with exact absolute-rational error comparison. Tie: smallest denominator; if still tied, numerically smaller rational. Invalid M<1 rejects; input is exact rational, not an untyped ADC float.

positivity.why: Pi decimal entered as exact rational, not an assumed transcendental exact Pi

falsifiers: Returning 3/2 when M=1 must fail, even though exact source denominator is 2.
For x=1/2, M=1, returning 1 instead of 0 must fail (halfway integer tie).
Using floating point to compare candidate errors may reverse sufficiently close rational order; only exact rational comparison is accepted.
Returning a nonreduced or negative-denominator result violates the canonical output contract.
